title: Joint Attention & Secure Social Referencing
goal: Explore joint Attention & Secure Social Referencing at a comfortable, adaptable level.
readiness: Baby is comfortable, interested and able to try the steps with the stated support. Follow current readiness rather than completing earlier activities. Stop when baby disengages.
steps: Sit with the infant on the floor and introduce a novel, benign object (e.g., a textured mechanical wind-up toy) slightly out of reach.
Point at the object and say, 'Look! What's that?' to establish joint visual gaze.

Provide an encouraging nod, warm smile, and soothing vocal confirmation ('It's okay, you can touch it!').
completionCriteria: Caregiver and child share interest in an object, using looking, pointing, sounds or another cue.
safety: Ensure all novelty items are completely safe, nontoxic, and free of choking hazards.
adaptations: Make the activity shorter or easier and offer more support.

benefits: Offers voluntary practice with shared attention, connection and expressing preferences or feelings.
